conventions.convention: The Coxeter matrix has finite generating set S; W need not be finite. Right weak order means v=ux with additive length, left weak order means v=xu. D_L tests multiplication on the left and D_R on the right.
N(w) consists of positive roots sent negative by w. Right weak order uses containment of N(w inverse); left weak order uses containment of N(w). Prefix roots belong to N(w inverse).

Arbitrary meets and bounded joins in general weak order are asserted for nonempty subsets. In finite W, the empty meet is w0 and the empty join is 1. The empty simple-generator subset has W_empty={1} and join 1.
A linear extension lists every element exactly once, respecting the strict partial order; the empty poset has the empty extension.

Heaps are defined for arbitrary words. Earlier positions generate dependencies for equal labels or m≥3, including infinity; commutations require m=2. Full commutativity concerns all reduced words of an element.

The heap criterion requires both absence of convex alternating chains of finite length m≥3 and absence of equal-label covering pairs. Reducedness is a conclusion; pairs with m=infinity impose no forbidden-chain condition.

The Cambrian construction assumes finite type and right weak order. Equivalence means equality of sortable-projection images; class order is the order on those images. 'Cambrian quotient' denotes this kernel construction, without identification with the least oriented rank-two contraction congruence.

The upper map is u_c(w)=pi_(c inverse)(w w0) w0, with multiplication by w0 on the right. A projection indexed by a parabolic Coxeter element is formed within that parabolic, using its own longest element.
The A3 calculation uses labels 1,2,3,4, s_i=(i i+1), right-to-left composition and one-line values in argument order; right multiplication swaps adjacent positions.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite Coxeter matrix, both weak orders are partial orders with minimum 1; inversion is an order isomorphism between them. Right covers are exactly v=us with length rising by one, every comparison is a chain of covers, and intervals are finite and graded by shifted length. For all u,v, u≤_R v iff N(u inverse)⊆N(v inverse), and u≤_L v iff N(u)⊆N(v); both inversion-set cardinalities equal length.

u≤_R v iff some reduced expression of v begins with a reduced expression of u. If s is a left descent of both u and v, then u≤_R v iff su≤_R sv. For u≤_R v, x↦ux is an order isomorphism [1,u inverse v]_R→[u,v]_R with additive length; the symmetric left-order statements also hold.

In either weak order every nonempty subset has a meet, and a nonempty subset has a join iff bounded above, with join equal to the meet of its upper bounds. For finite W, both orders are lattices with minimum 1 and maximum w0. For J⊆S, W_J is finite iff J has an upper bound iff its join exists; then its join is w0(J) in both orders, including J=empty.

For every word s, L(P_s,s)=C(s). The labeled-word map on linear extensions is injective. Two words are commutation-equivalent iff their heaps are isomorphic as labeled posets, with each j-th label occurrence matched to the j-th occurrence. Thus a fully commutative element has a heap well defined up to labeled isomorphism.

For finite-type W and a Coxeter element c, every nonempty set A of c-sortable elements has a c-sortable meet and join; N((meet A) inverse)=intersection of N(a inverse) over a∈A. For every x,y∈W, pi_c preserves their meet and join. Its kernel is a lattice congruence, and the sortable quotient is lattice-isomorphic to the sortable sublattice.

An element is fully commutative iff no reduced word contains a full alternating factor of length m(u,v) for a distinct pair with 3≤m(u,v)<infinity. For an arbitrary word s, its heap avoids both convex alternating chains of these lengths and equal-label covering pairs iff s is reduced and its represented element is fully commutative.

For fully commutative w and a reduced word with heap P, the map x↦I(x) is an order isomorphism [1,w]_R→J(P). The ideal is independent of the reduced word of x, has cardinality length(x), and carries interval meets and joins to intersection and union. Consequently this right weak interval is a finite distributive lattice.

For all x,y, their common lower bounds form a finite set, and every member of maximal length is their meet. Every nonempty subset has a meet, obtained by a strictly length-decreasing finite meet procedure. Every nonempty bounded-above subset has join equal to the meet of its upper bounds. The left-order analogues hold, without Choice.

If x has every simple generator as a left descent, then N(x inverse)=Phi_positive, W is finite, and x is its longest element. For J⊆S and w∈W_J, if every s∈J lowers w on the left, then W_J is finite and w=w0(J). No Choice is used.

Every finite poset has a linear extension. Every linear extension of an order ideal extends to one of the whole poset with that ideal first. Any two linear extensions are connected by finitely many swaps of consecutive incomparable entries.

For finite-type W, u_c(w)=pi_(c inverse)(w w0)w0 is monotone and idempotent, with w≤_R u_c(w). The fibers of u_c and pi_c agree; pi_c u_c=pi_c and u_c pi_c=u_c. Each fiber is exactly [pi_c(w),u_c(w)]_R.

Intervals and local finiteness.
Chains and the convex-chain linear-extension lemma.
Minimal/maximal elements in finite-poset extension arguments.
Lattices, distributivity and downward-closed order ideals.
Finite J(P), with intersection as meet and union as join.

Positivity of cos(pi/3).
cos(pi/2)=0 in the A2 computation.
Congruence compatibility, proposed quotient operations and class endpoints.

Sortable iff aligned, and sortable parabolic restriction.

Monotonicity, greatest-sortable-below, both directions of the full cone criterion and parabolic compatibility.
Projection interface, skip basis and the chamber union indexed by a projection fiber.
Right-to-left permutation composition and one-line notation in the A3 calculations.

seams_checked.note: Descents and the factorization w=w_J d retain their specified sides and additive length. The full-descent argument uses the invariant subsystem Phi_J=Phi∩V_J and explicitly identifies its intrinsic representation.
Longest-element properties are invoked only after finiteness is assumed or proved. Finite-parabolic longest elements and length-complement identities retain the supplier hypotheses.

The forbidden-chain theorem F3 states braid connectivity and M-reducedness explicitly. It uses braid moves followed by adjacent equal-letter cancellation, and imposes no braid condition for infinite labels.

This is a declared background prerequisite with no congruence or chain-label proposition consumed by the heap proofs. The distributive interval theorem uses the earlier order-ideal lattice supplier directly.

Owned facts preserve finite type, right weak order, actual parabolic prefixes, oriented alignment and both directions of the cone criterion. Chamber unions are correctly indexed by group elements in a projection fiber.

The endpoint theorem F16 states the interval-class hypothesis and the iff between congruence and monotone endpoints. Its application follows the proof that the fibers are intervals; quotient operations retain representative independence.

The growth theorem F3 quotes the parabolic full-descent criterion with x∈W_J and every s∈J lowering length. Proof 1.1 applies it to the parabolic factor or its inverse, rather than directly to an arbitrary ambient element.

The incoming facts retain N(w inverse) for right weak order, the left-descent root test, simple-generator covers, finite lattice hypotheses and the common-left-descent translation condition. Translation for two ascents is explicitly derived by applying the cited descent statement to their left multiples.
